But C4, which checks for the refrigerator-inspection coordination action, failed. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the settlement's commitment encodes the inspection notice as a 'schedule_update' rather than matching whatever field name or action-type string C4 expects for the 'refrigerator-inspection coordination action.' The group attempted to use PF1's coordination requirement but the check does not recognize the encoding. P1 passed in both settled rollouts (tally 2/2), so provenance for PF1 is working. C1 and C2 passed in both settled rollouts (tally 2/2 each). Rollouts 0 and 2 both auto-failed on the turn cap at 10 turns without settling. In both, PF1 and PF2 were revealed early (rollout 0: turns 1-2; rollout 2: turns 2-3), so disclosure was not the problem. In rollout 0, A1 and the group reached apparent consensus on a schedule by turns 6-8 but never issued a settle action, continuing to exchange confirmations through turn 9. In rollout 2, A1 refused to settle, insisting on external facilities-team confirmation about whether the Room 1 inspection takes the whole room offline — information no agent possesses — and the conversation deadlocked through turn 9. This is a STRUCTURAL problem with the settle-eligibility condition: A1's decision-maker persona is gating settlement on resolving an ambiguity (full-room vs. refrigerator-only impact of the inspection) that the scenario does not give any agent the information to resolve, so the settle-eligibility condition rarely triggers even when all decisive facts have been disclosed.
